newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Hun Sen backer claims to head Cambodia U.N. mission.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen backer claims to head Cambodia U.N. mission.

text.p: Cambodia's deputy U.N. representative, Ouch Borith, claimed on Tuesday that he now headed his country's U.N. mission in place of Ambassador Prince Sisowath Sirirath, a supporter of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Ranariddh was deposed in a July 6 coup by then Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

Ouch said he had been appointed by the authorities in Phnom Penh as charge d'affaires of the mission pending the naming of a new permanent representative. But he conceded he was still working from home as he had not been able to take over the mission premises.
Ouch told a news conference that Sisowath had defied an order by acting head of state Chea Sim to terminate his appointment in New York and return to Cambodia "to assume a new assignment."

"Thus, not only did he defy the legal authority of the government in Phnom Penh, which continues to enjoy the diplomatic recognition of all members of the United Nations, but he took it upon himself to falsely and deceitfully inform permanent representatives that his removal and my appointment as charge d'affaires were not valid."

Although the manager of the building housing Cambodia's U.N. mission had received letters from Phnom Penh telling him not to regard Sisowath and other staff as diplomats, he said he was "awaiting instructions from the (U.S.) State Department and the United Nations," Ouch said.

"Pending such instructions, I have indeed been forced to work from my home as I refuse to be drawn into a physical fight with the illegal occupants of the Cambodian mission, something that is alien to the culture of Cambodia," he said.

"Not only did the ambassador obstruct my work, but he continued to confuse my colleagues, the distinguished permanent representatives and distinguished U.N. secretariat officers, by instructing the non-Cambodian secretary of the mission to falsely inform persons who called me that I "no longer work there," Ouch added.
A member of the Cambodian U.N. mission, whose current members support Norodom Ranariddh, said Ambassador Sisowath was now on a visit to California.
